methodology: Bounded preliminary verse-by-verse comparison with the Exodus court contest and later naming/interpretation traditions. Primary critical editions, recension history, and precise stable source URLs not independently collated in this session. Leads are nonpublic; no borrowing or historical dependence claim. Previous open PR #266 covers 7:111–115; do not count it again.

records.topic: Magicians cast and enchant the spectators' eyes
records.notes: Qur'an describes visual enchantment and fear; Exodus describes Egyptian practitioners' rods becoming serpents through secret arts, without the explicit 'bewitching eyes' phrase.
records.pending_question: Compare Hebrew ḥarṭummîm and Qur'anic siḥr; check whether 2 Timothy's Jannes and Jambres tradition contributes only names, not this event.

records.topic: Moses' staff swallows the magicians' devices
records.notes: Shared striking narrative action: a divinely authorized staff swallows rival practitioners' staffs. Exodus assigns the court demonstration to Aaron, while Qur'an 7:117 addresses Moses; Qur'an here calls the rivals' items what they fabricated.
records.pending_question: Collate MT and LXX Exodus 7:12, Qur'anic Arabic 7:117, and possible ancient Jewish retellings; note actor, objects, and chronology.

records.topic: Truth is established and their works rendered void
records.notes: Qur'an explicitly interprets the contest as truth defeating falsehood; Exodus reports the swallowed staffs and Pharaoh's hardened heart; later Egyptian magicians acknowledge divine agency in Exodus 8:19, at a different plague episode.
records.pending_question: Avoid collapsing Exodus 7 and 8 into one event; examine how later exegetes interpret the distinction.

records.notes: A broad narrative consequence of the contest; Exodus describes the staff's victory but not this verse's explicit collective humiliation of the magicians.
records.pending_question: Check pre-Islamic narrative witnesses before assigning any stronger speech/action equivalence.

records.notes: Qur'an portrays the magicians prostrating after the contest; Exodus does not narrate their prostration or conversion. Exodus 8:19 has magicians recognize God's power in a later episode; 2 Timothy names opponents of Moses without this response.
records.pending_question: Seek securely pre-Islamic Jewish, Christian, Syriac or other retellings with prostration; do not assert equivalence with Exodus 8:19.

pending_questions: Collate Exodus 7:10–13 MT and LXX and date the witnesses; evaluate 8:19 separately.
